methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series D → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.5x) to $1.6B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.0B - $2.3B.

private.name: Exotec
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Series D), post-money $2B

data.narrative:
Hadrian, a Series D robotics and manufacturing company founded by Chris Power, is valued at $1.6B post-money following $1.37B in total capital raised. The valuation is benchmarked against a peer set of four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies spanning Series C to Series E, supplemented by a broader universe of eight private robotics firms and one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach, which applies a typical 1.5x step-up multiplier from Series D forward, implies a valuation of $2.4B. The peer-median method, drawing from four direct comparables (Divergent at $2.3B, Exotec at $2.0B, Agile Robots at $1.0B, and Nimble Robotics at $1.0B), yields a median of $1.5B with a range of $1.0B to $2.3B. These methods reflect different but complementary signals: stage-based momentum versus current peer pricing.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $1.3B (low) to $2.8B (high), with a median of $1.9B. The current $1.6B valuation sits near the lower bound of this range. Key uncertainties include the applicability of the stage-progression multiplier given market conditions and the representativeness of the four-company peer median in a nascent, heterogeneous sector. Revenue growth, unit economics, and path to profitability would be critical to validating positioning within this band.
